newsitem.title: CHILE: New charges against head of German colony in Chile.
newsitem.headline: New charges against head of German colony in Chile.

text.p: New charges of child abuse and tax evasion have been leveled against the fugitive leader of a German colony in the Andes, but Chilean police have still been unable to locate him, papers reported on Sunday.
Ana Rodriguez, a neighbour of the Colonia Dignidad German community, said her 10 year-old son was submitted to abuse by founder Paul Schaeffer while at a boarding-school in the enclave.
The boy, identified by the initials J.E.B.R., told local daily La Tercera that he was forced to let Schaeffer bathe and touch him.
The child will be taken to Santiago for physical and psychological examination before formalising charges against Schaeffer, who is said to be between 78 and 80.
The family's lawyer, Hernan Fernandez, told reporters he was studying two other cases of families who had come forward with accusations of child molestation against Schaeffer.

The deputy head of Chile's Internal Tax Service, Bernardo Lara, told reporters on Saturday that Colonia Dignidad (Dignity Colony) faced 27 charges of tax evasion for up to 600 million pesos ($1.4 million).

An arrest warrant was issued against former Nazi army officer last year after parents of at least five boys who attended a boarding school in the colony filed charges of sexual abuse and illegal detention of the children by Schaeffer and other colony officials.

Chilean police have made four inspections of the compound without being able to trace Schaeffer. Followers said last week Schaeffer was not at the sprawling settlement and would sooner commit suicide than give up.
Schaeffer set up the colony in the Andean foothills about 200 miles (320 km) south of Santiago around 1960 after fleeing Germany where he was charged with molesting boys at an orphanage he founded.
The community was formed as a non-profit organisation offering medical assistance and a boarding school for local communities.
